title: The Green Hill Solar Farm Order 2026
summary: This Order authorises Green Hill Solar Farm Limited (referred to in this Order as the undertaker) to construct, operate, maintain and decommission a ground mounted solar photovoltaic generating station with a gross electrical output capacity over 100 megawatts and associated development. The Order would permit the undertaker to acquire, compulsorily or by agreement, land and rights in land and to use land for this purpose.

title: The Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026 (Age of Sale Notices and Consequential Amendments) (Wales) Regulations 2026 / Rheoliadau Deddf Tybaco a Fêps 2026 (Hysbysiadau Oedran Gwerthu a Diwygiadau Canlyniadol) (Cymru) 2026
summary:
Section 1 of the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026 (“the 2026 Act”) changes the required age at which an individual can legally be sold tobacco products from an individual aged 18 or over, to an individual born before 1 January 2009. Under section 6 (1) of the 2026 Act, tobacco retailers in Wales must display a notice on their premises that contains the statements in section 6 (2) of that Act to reflect the new age of sale requirement. Regulation 2 prescribes the minimum size requirements for such a notice, and regulation 3 prescribes the minimum size of the statements to be contained in that notice.

Mae adran 1 o Ddeddf Tybaco a Fêps 2026 (“Deddf 2026”) yn newid yr oedran gofynnol y caniateir i gynhyrchion tybaco gael eu gwerthu yn gyfreithlon i unigolyn, o unigolyn sy’n 18 oed neu drosodd i unigolyn a anwyd cyn 1 Ionawr 2009. O dan adran 6 (1) o Ddeddf 2026, rhaid i fanwerthwyr tybaco yng Nghymru arddangos hysbysiad yn eu mangreoedd sy’n cynnwys y datganiadau yn adran 6(2) o’r Ddeddf honno er mwyn adlewyrchu’r gofyniad oedran gwerthu newydd. Mae rheoliad 2 yn rhagnodi’r gofynion maint lleiaf ar gyfer hysbysiad o’r fath, ac mae rheoliad 3 yn rhagnodi maint lleiaf y datganiadau sydd i’w cynnwys yn yr hysbysiad hwnnw.

title: The County Borough of the Vale of Glamorgan (Electoral Arrangements) Order 2026 / Gorchymyn Bwrdeistref Sirol Bro Morgannwg (Trefniadau Etholiadol) 2026
summary: This Order implements the recommendations of the Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru (“the Commission”), which reported in January 2026 on its review of the electoral arrangements for the County Borough of the Vale of Glamorgan. The Commission’s report proposed an increase in the number of electoral wards from 24 to 26 and an increase in the number of councillors from 58 to 59.

title: The County Borough of Caerphilly (Electoral Arrangements) Order 2026 / Gorchymyn Bwrdeistref Sirol Caerffili (Trefniadau Etholiadol) 2026
summary: This Order implements the recommendations of the Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru (“the Commission”), which reported in March 2026 on its review of the electoral arrangements for the County Borough of Caerphilly. The Commission’s report proposed a reduction in the number of electoral wards from 31 to 30 and a decrease in the number of councillors from 69 to 68.

title: The County of Carmarthenshire (Electoral Arrangements) Order 2026 / Gorchymyn Sir Gaerfyrddin (Trefniadau Etholiadol) 2026
summary: This Order implements the recommendations of the Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru (“the Commission”), which reported in January 2026 on its review of the electoral arrangements for the County of Carmarthenshire. The Commission’s report proposed a reduction in the number of electoral wards from 51 to 47 and a decrease in the number of councillors from 75 to 74. The Commission’s report also recommended consequential changes to electoral arrangements for the County of Carmarthenshire as a result of changes to community boundaries that have already been implemented.

title: The Insolvency (Amendment) (2026 Act) (Commencement No. 1 and Transitional Provisions) Order (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: This Order is the first commencement order made under the Insolvency (Amendment) Act (Northern Ireland) 2026 (“the 2026 Act”).

title: The Steeple Renewables Project Order 2026
summary: This Order grants development consent for, and authorises the construction, operation and maintenance of a solar generating station and battery energy storage facility together with associated development. This Order imposes requirements in connection with the development and authorises the compulsory purchase of land (including rights in land) and the right to use land and to override easements and other rights.

title: Correction Slip
summary: These Regulations make provision in relation to the recovery of debt under Schedules 3ZA and 3ZB to the Social Security Administration Act 1992 (c. 5) (“the Act”), as inserted by the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 (c. 28) (“2025 Act”).

title: The Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) Order 2019 (S.I. 2019/183) (“the 2019 Order”) to remove reference to the Scottish Ministers’ functions under section 44 of the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009 (asp 12), because there are no functions under section 44 that could be exercised by way of arrangements under section 93 of the Scotland Act 1998 (c. 46).

title: The Scottish Administration (Offices) Order 2026
summary: This Order specifies the Clerk of the Sexual Offences Court and Deputy Clerks of the Sexual Offences Court as offices in the Scottish Administration which are not ministerial offices for the purposes of the Scotland Act 1998.

title: The School Teachers’ Pay and Conditions (England) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes provision for the determination of the remuneration of school teachers (within the meaning of section 122 of the Education Act 2002 (c. 32)) in England and other conditions of employment of school teachers which relate to their professional duties and working time.

title: The Diocese of Leicester (Educational Endowments) (Hathern Church of England Primary School Teacher’s House) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the Leicester Diocesan Board of Education as trustee of the foundation known as Hathern Church of England Primary School Teacher’s House and makes new provision as to the use of that foundation. It creates a separate foundation for the purpose of providing religious education in accordance with the doctrines of the Church of England within the Parish of Hathern. The Order provides for the Religious Education Fund to be held on trust by the minister and churchwardens for the time being of the Parish of Hathern.

title: The Crime and Policing Act 2026 (Commencement No. 4) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force specified provisions of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 (c. 20) (“the Act”). These are the fourth commencement regulations made under the Act.

title: The Official Controls (Plant Protection Products) (Amendment) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Official Controls (Plant Protection Products) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2020 (S.R. 2020 No.360) (“PPP Official Controls Regulations”)

title: The Building (Local Authority Charges and Amendments Relating to Charging) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations set out provisions in relation to charges of local authorities for or in connection with certain building related functions.

title: The Welfare Food (Amendment) (England and Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Welfare Food Regulations 1996 (S.I. 1996/1434) (“the 1996 Regulations”). The 1996 Regulations provide for a scheme (the “Nursery Milk Scheme”) which entitles children under the age of five years to one-third of a pint of milk (189ml) on any day where they are provided with childcare, by an approved childcare provider, for two hours or more. Regulations 3 to 10 amend the 1996 Regulations to replace references to day care with childcare and to update references to childcare legislation in England and Wales which have been updated since the 1996 Regulations came into force. These include changes made by the Childcare Act 2006 (c. 21) for England, and the Children and Families (Wales) Measure 2010 (nawm 1) and the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Wales) Order 2010 (S.I. 2010/2839) (W.233)) for Wales. These Regulations also extend eligibility under the Nursery Milk Scheme to childcare providers registered with Childminder Agencies. Those providers will be able to claim reimbursement for milk they provide to eligible children in their care in the same way as childcare providers that are currently registered with Ofsted, or for providers registered with the Welsh Ministers in Wales. These Regulations also make provision in consequence of the repeal and replacement of the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Wales) Order 2010 with the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Revocation and Transitional Provision) (Wales) Order 2026 (S.I. 2026/100).

title: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) (Amendment No. 2) Order 2026
summary: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) Order 2010 (S.I. 2010/2655) (“the 2010 Order”) organises the First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal into chambers and makes provision for the allocation of those tribunals’ functions between the chambers.
